topic: Massage for musicians' necks and shoulders

slides.headline: Long rehearsals leaving your neck tight?
slides.sub: Guitar, violin, piano or drums: where massage fits for musicians.

slides.title: Why musicians tighten up
slides.body: Playing means hours of small, repeated movements in one position: chin on a violin, head tilted over keys, one shoulder lifted to the fretboard. The neck and shoulders often feel it first.

slides.title: What massage can help with
slides.body: Remedial massage can ease the tight, heavy feeling in your neck, shoulders and upper back, and help you feel more relaxed around busy performance weeks. Effects tend to be short-term, so pair it with movement.

slides.title: Micro-breaks in rehearsal
slides.body: Every 20 to 30 minutes, put the instrument down, roll your shoulders, gently turn your head side to side and shake out your hands. A minute is enough, and it adds up over a long session.

slides.title: Build capacity, not just looseness
slides.body: Upper back and shoulder strengthening, like band rows and wall slides, helps you hold your instrument for longer with less fatigue. Our physios can tailor this to how you play.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Numbness, tingling or weakness in the hands, pain that lingers long after playing, or losing fine control are worth a physio or GP assessment rather than more massage.

slides.headline: Book a session between gigs
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physiotherapy work with our physios, so hands-on care can fit into a bigger plan. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Long rehearsals leaving your neck and shoulders tight? 🎻

Playing an instrument means hours of small, repeated movements in one position. Chin on the violin, head over the keys, a shoulder lifted to the fretboard. It's no surprise the neck and shoulders often complain first.

Remedial massage can ease that tight, heavy feeling and help you feel more relaxed around busy performance weeks. The effect is usually short-term, so it works well alongside micro-breaks every 20 to 30 minutes and some upper back strengthening.

Numbness, tingling, hand weakness or losing fine control is worth a physio or GP assessment first.
